description: Second independent run, same setup as E0b (n=128, 1 replication), this time caching the generated motions/metadata and running length/caption diagnostics. Generated motions cached to e0b_generated_cache/ for future re-analysis without regenerating.

diagnostic.conclusion: Length distribution matches ground truth closely (means within 0.7 frames); all 128 captions unique (no duplication); caption-to-motion pairing at scoring time verified correct by code inspection (CompMDMGeneratedDataset.__getitem__ reuses the exact same caption/tokens dict entry created during generation). None of SUP-21's three cheapest leads (length, caption uniqueness, caption-motion pairing) explain the discrepancy.

comparison_to_v1_run.note: v1 and v2 differ slightly in exact numbers (e.g. GT R-Prec-top3 0.7969 vs 0.8125), plausibly because v2's added diagnostic gt_loader iteration consumed random state differently before gt_loader's own shuffle=True draw, changing batch composition slightly between runs. The QUALITATIVE pattern is stable across both independent runs: generated R-Precision-top3 (v1: 0.7578, v2: 0.7578 -- identical) well above the published 0.611, generated FID (v1: 1.0731, v2: 1.3997 -- both far above) well above the published 0.544. This stability across two independent runs further rules out single-replication noise as the explanation (consistent with a separately reported 20-replication spread, 0.5323-0.7114, which does not reach either of our values).

verdict: FAIL, both runs. Leading cheap hypotheses (length distribution, caption duplication, caption-motion pairing) all ruled out. Remaining candidate: this project's 128-sample subset was selected as the first rows in HF streaming order, not a random draw from the full ~4384-sequence test set -- not yet directly tested.
